ippu captures your device notifications to a local database and forwards them, in batches, to a webhook you configure. It is built to be lightweight and battery-friendly: notifications are captured event-driven (no background polling), and uploads are deferred and batched.

v1.32 — Message notifications now have actions: a one-time code gets a "Copy" button, other messages get inline "Reply" (sent via ariy), and both offer "Mark as read" — all without opening the app.

v1.31 — Fixed: the compose button on Messages was hidden below the screen until you scrolled — it's now pinned above the tab bar and always visible.

v1.30 — Removed the temporary "Clear received messages" button now that the inbox repush is done.

v1.29 — Encrypted Backup & restore (Settings): save your settings and message history to Drive, OneDrive, or local storage through the system file picker, protected by a passphrase. Restore it on this or a new device. Also: the Pairing screen (formerly "Relay") now matches ariy's — same layout, order, and wording — and generating the shared key lives only here, where it belongs.

v1.28 — Recover from a relay gap: ariy gained a "Repush entire inbox" button that re-sends every SMS so this device can rebuild its history, and this device gained a "Clear received messages" button (Settings → Relay) to wipe received messages first for a clean rebuild. Duplicates are dropped by content hash.

v1.27 — Messages now keep their real order: a relayed message is timestamped by when the SMS actually arrived on the sender phone, not when the push reached this device — so a delayed or synced message slots into the correct place in the conversation instead of jumping to the bottom.

v1.26 — New Diagnostics screen (Settings → Diagnostics): every inbound push and compose is logged with the reason when it fails — decrypt failures, stale token, not paired, HTTP codes — so problems are visible instead of silent. Duplicate messages from the missed-SMS sync are now ignored.

v1.25 — Large collapsing headers on every tab: the title starts big and shrinks into the toolbar as you scroll, like Google Messages.

v1.24 — Material 3 Expressive visual refresh.

v1.23 — Search now closes on Back (and with the ✕) instead of exiting the app, and only queries once you pause typing. Under the hood: the conversation list no longer decrypts settings on every row, and theme colours are resolved once — lighter on CPU and battery.

v1.22 — Compose screen reworked to a Google Messages layout: a recipient row up top and the message bar pinned to the bottom, with a SIM selector inline. Settings and Status are now a single coherent flat design (section headers, no mismatched cards), which also fixes the grey blocks in AMOLED.

v1.21 — Reworked the chat thread to a Google Messages style: consecutive messages from one side group into a single connected shape, and a centered time appears above each cluster instead of a timestamp on every bubble.

v1.20 — Redesigned the compose screen (labelled fields, inline contact picker, SIM selector, send button). AMOLED dark mode is now truly black across the Status and Settings cards, not just the background.

v1.19 — Mute a conversation (long-press it in the list) to stop its notifications while still receiving messages as unread. New AMOLED dark theme (Appearance → Pure black) for true-black surfaces on OLED screens. Fixed: tapping a message notification, then Back, now returns to the conversation list instead of the home screen.

v1.18 — Read & unread: unread conversations show in bold with a count badge, and the Messages tab carries a total-unread badge; opening a chat marks it read. Further chat polish — a rounded compose field with a circular send button, and tidier bubble sizing, alignment, and spacing.

v1.17 — Redesigned chat UI: colored contact avatars in the conversation list, cleaner message bubbles with the accent colour for your replies, inline timestamps, and Today/Yesterday date separators.

v1.16 — Reverse pairing by QR: ariy now shows a QR of its own token, and this screen can scan it — no more copying the token across by hand.

v1.15 — Renamed to ippu (the companion sender app is now ariy), with new wordmark icons. Message management: long-press any message to copy, select text, forward, or delete it. Tapping a message notification now opens that exact conversation with the message highlighted. New compose screen — pick a contact or type a number and choose which SIM ariy sends from.

v1.14 — Reverse direction: compose a message here and have the sender phone send it from its SIM, over the same encrypted channel.

v1.13 — New Messages tab: relayed messages are saved and shown as a searchable chat history. Fixes: app icon no longer clipped on some launchers; text fields now stay above the keyboard.

v1.12 — New wordmark app icon (adapts to light/dark and Material You). Relayed messages now show which SIM they arrived on (e.g. “+9715… on e&”).

v1.11 — Receive relayed messages: a new “Relay (receive)” screen lets a companion app (ariy) push you notifications — e.g. forwarded SMS — over end-to-end encrypted FCM. Pair by scanning a QR.

v1.10 — The Apps and “Keywords & notes” screens open much faster: app icons now load row by row as you scroll, instead of every icon being read before anything appears.

v1.9 — The Apps and “Keywords & notes” screens now show a loading spinner while your app list is read, instead of looking empty.

v1.8 — Per-app keywords & notes: log only the notifications matching your keywords, and append a note to what gets logged.

v1.7 — Bottom-nav layout (Status / Settings / About), settings menu with focused screens, and an Appearance section (theme mode + Default/Material color).

v1.6 — Blue theme matching the app icon, for better visibility (follows system light/dark).

v1.5 — Faster capture & upload (less CPU/battery); change notes here; standard back navigation.

v1.4 — New app icon, splash screen, About & Help screens.

v1.3 — Ignore duplicate notifications (content + time window).

v1.2 — Material 3 redesign; choose which apps to capture.

v1.1 — UI fixes; clearer auth setup; show-token toggle.

v1.0 — Initial release.

1. Tap “Grant notification access” and enable ippu in the system list — this lets the app see notifications.\n2. Tap “Ignore battery optimization” so uploads run reliably.\nWithout notification access, nothing is captured.

Enter your Webhook URL and the auth token. The token is sent as a header: by default “Authorization: Bearer <token>”. For a custom Header Auth credential, set the Auth header name to “key” and clear the prefix so the raw token is sent. Tap the eye icon to reveal the token. Use an https URL — content is sensitive.
Under “Included apps”, tap “Choose apps” to pick which apps to capture. If you select none, all apps are captured. Selecting apps limits capture to just those.

Settings → “Keywords & notes” lists every app you selected under Apps. Against each app you can set:

• Keywords — a comma-separated list, e.g. “delivered, out for delivery”. Only notifications containing one of them (in the title, text or subtext, case-insensitive) are logged. Leave it empty to log every notification from that app.

• Notes — optional free text appended, on a new line, to the logged notification's text field. Useful for tagging a source, e.g. “work phone”. Notes are added even in metadata-only mode, since you wrote them yourself.

Excluded keywords under Privacy still win: a notification matching one is dropped regardless of these rules.
Some apps re-post the same notification repeatedly. “Ignore duplicate window” drops identical content from the same app seen within that many seconds (default one day). Set 0 to keep every copy.
Choose when uploads run: Periodic (every N minutes, min 15), Threshold (after N pending), or Manual (“Sync now” only). Optionally restrict to Wi-Fi or to charging to save battery/data.

Turn off “Capture notification body” to store metadata only. Add excluded keywords to drop notifications containing sensitive words (e.g. OTP). “Retention days” controls how long uploaded rows are kept before purging.

• 403 on upload: the auth header/token is wrong — for custom Header Auth use header name “key” and an empty prefix.\n• Nothing captured: grant notification access; check your included-apps selection.\n• Uploads delayed: allow the app to ignore battery optimization, or use “Sync now”.

For each app, log only the notifications containing one of the keywords. Leave keywords empty to log everything from that app. Notes are appended to the logged notification\'s text.
